$Comment: SummaryHud.Position is a shared-library HudPosition preset id, authored PascalCase like every other id in this schema (e.g. 'TopCenter'). Matching is case- and underscore-insensitive, so 'TOP_CENTER' resolves to the same preset. SummaryHud.Color is the colour the panel's frame is drawn in, a hex that multiplies the shipped frame: #ffffff is exactly the shipped look, a darker hex darkens it, a hue tints it, and eight digits carry a transparency in the last two (#ffffffb8 is about 72 percent). It is left out here on purpose: absent, the panel takes the look every HUD card on this server shares, Ziggfreed Common's Server/ZiggfreedCommon/HudCards/Default.json (owner layer mods/ziggfreedcommon/hud-cards.json), so one file dims every card at once; state it here only to treat this panel differently. The Limits group is deliberately NOT authored here: every ceiling under it means unlimited when absent, and the right ceiling depends on a server's own player count and hardware, so shipping numbers would impose a guess on everyone. A busy server adds e.g. 'Limits': { 'MaxSessionsPerWorld': 60, 'MaxPuppetsPerWorld': 40, 'MaxStashesPerSection': 8 }; each knob is independent and any one may be set on its own. MaxStashesPerSection caps how many blocks in one 32x32x32 chunk section may hold placed station input; topping up material already placed is never denied, and a multiblock structure's own activation mark never counts against the ceiling. Limits.UnattendedIntervalMs paces each world's unattended pass (stations whose action authors Work.Unattended settling with nobody engaged, plus the placed-item display rebuild after a chunk loads) and defaults to 1000ms when absent; raise it to settle in coarser, cheaper bursts - the settled amounts come out the same either way. Limits.MaxUnattendedGatherCycles caps how many accrued unattended cycles ONE gather pays out, server-wide: the effective ceiling is the smaller of it and each action's own Work.Unattended.MaxCycles, so it tightens payouts without raising any action's ceiling; absent means each action's own ceiling alone applies. Moments is the engine-wide default cue layer, keyed by moment id exactly like an action's own Moments map, and sits UNDER every action's entry for the same id per leaf (the action's authored leaves win, the leaves it omits fall through to here). The one entry shipped, 'refused', is what every turned-away press answers with - the same SoundEvent the vanilla processing benches play when they cannot proceed - so a station with no refusal cue of its own still sounds like it heard you. Dress one reason differently with a 'refused:<reason>' entry (refused:no_materials, refused:wrong_tool, refused:occupied, ...; the reason is the tail of the notice's own key), which overlays 'refused' per leaf; author 'Sounds': [] to silence one. A refusal cue plays at once, so a DelayMs on it reads as zero. Refusals.RepeatWindowMs (default 1500) is how long the same player pressing the same station again for the same reason is answered by the sound alone - no second notice, no second particle burst or camera shake; 0 answers every press in full.
